name: GW energy flux F = c^3 omega^2 h^2/(16 pi G) relating strain to luminosity

source.located: The GW energy-flux formula of linearised GR in the short-wave (Isaacson) regime: Maggiore, Gravitational Waves Vol. 1 (OUP 2007) eqs. 1.135-1.136, 1.146, 1.151, 1.153 (Isaacson 1968 behind it). published_statement: Gerosa L01 p.5, G = c = 1, eq. (1.153): 'dE/(dA dt) = +t^00 = (1/32 pi) <hdot^TT_ij hdot^TT_ij> = (1/16 pi) <hdot_+^2 + hdot_x^2>'; boxed: 'dE/dt = (r^2/32 pi) \int dOmega <hdot^TT_ij hdot^TT_ij>' ('GW energy flux'), obtained from t^00 = (1/32pi)<hdot^TT_ij hdot^TT_ij> = (1/16pi)<hdot_+^2 + hdot_x^2> (1.135-1.136), t^0r (1.146) and the far-field form h^TT_ij(t,r) = (1/r) f_ij(t - r/c) (p.4-5). With G and c restored: F = c^3/(16 pi G) <hdot_+^2 + hdot_x^2>. L03 p.2 (Maggiore 3.330-3.336) gives, for a rotating quadrupole (binary on a fixed circular orbit), h_+ ~ (1+cos^2 theta)/2 cos(2 w_s t_ret), h_x ~ cos theta sin(2 w_s t_ret), 'face-on: circular polarisation; edge-on: linear polarisation h_+', dP/dOmega = (r^2/16pi)<hdot_+^2 + hdot_x^2> with the pattern [((1+cos^2 theta)/2)^2 + cos^2 theta], 'Emission is largest in the direction perpendicular to the orbital plane'. The single-amplitude form F = c^3 w^2 h^2/(16 pi G) used by the tree is NOT printed in the source read; it follows from (1.153) only when h^2 = <h_+^2 + h_x^2> (e.g. circular polarisation of peak h in each polarisation).
published_hypotheses: Linearised GR about a background: g = gbar + h with a separation of scales, either lambda-bar << L_B or f_GW >> f_B (L01 p.2-3)
Short-wave (Isaacson) averaging over a length lbar with lambda-bar << lbar << L_B; t_mu_nu defined only as that average (L01 p.3, eqs. 1.122-1.130)
Away from the source (T_mu_nu = 0 at the evaluation point; nabla ~ partial) (L01 p.4)
Far zone: h^TT_ij = (1/r) f_ij(t - r/c) + O(1/r^2), i.e. outgoing radiation, r >> lambda (L01 p.4-5)
TT gauge / TT projection; two polarisations h_+, h_x (L01 p.4)
Four spacetime dimensions, massless spin-2 field propagating at c (implicit throughout: retarded time t - r/c)
For the angular pattern: quadrupole (slow-motion) approximation, source in the x-y plane rotating at w_s, radiating at 2 w_s (L03 p.2)
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED -- the polarisation content of h. branelink.py:204-206 writes the flux as c^3 w^2 h^2/(16 pi G) with a single h; the published form is c^3/(16 pi G)<hdot_+^2 + hdot_x^2>. The tree's form is exact iff h^2 = <h_+^2 + h_x^2> (total mean-square strain; = the per-polarisation peak for a circular wave). For a linearly polarised wave of peak amplitude h the flux is c^3 w^2 h^2/(32 pi G) (rederive check 3b), so reading the tree's h as a linear peak understates it by sqrt 2. branelink.py:209-211 (bulk_bits_per_watt) reuses the same h inside (h/h_n)^2 without saying which amplitude it is. A convention unstated, not an error: under the sky-rms reading it is exact (check 3a).

USED-FALSE-FOR-THE-SOURCE -- isotropic emission. branelink.py:204-206 and 214-217 put L/(4 pi D^2) at Proxima for the spinning rod (branelink.py:199-201). The rod's quadrupole is the binary's rotating quadrupole (check 2a-2b reproduces L03 p.2's pattern exactly), so its emission is anisotropic: flux at polar angle theta over the isotropic figure runs from 5/2 (face-on, along the spin axis) to 5/16 (edge-on) (check 4b). The tree's h is therefore the SKY-RMS strain, not the strain at Proxima, and the rod's axis relative to the Proxima line is never specified. The canonical entry names isotropy as a hypothesis; the owner's docstring does not say it is false for this source.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (15 checks, ~20 s). (1) For branelink's own rod quadrupole, the published flux c^3/(32 pi G)<hdot^TT_ij hdot^TT_ij> with the far-field strain (2G/(c^4 r)) Lambda Q'' (NAMED, not read), integrated over the sphere, equals G/(5c^5)<Q'''Q'''> = (2/45) G M^2 l^4 Omega^6/c^5 exactly -- the flux coefficient is the unique one consistent with the luminosity the tree seats. (2) The rod's h_+ ~ A0(1+cos^2 th)/2 cos 2 Omega t and h_x ~ A0 cos th sin 2 Omega t with A0 = G M l^2 Omega^2/(3 c^4 r): the source's binary pattern; <hdot^TT hdot^TT> = 2<hdot_+^2 + hdot_x^2> (1/32pi <-> 1/16pi). (3a) The tree's h^2 = 4 G L/(c^3 w^2 D^2) equals the SKY AVERAGE of <h_+^2 + h_x^2> exactly. (3b) linear polarisation of peak h: F = c^3 w^2 h^2/(32 pi G); (3c) circular of peak h: F = c^3 w^2 h^2/(16 pi G) -- the tree's form. (4) Face-on A0^2 = (5/2) h_tree^2; flux(theta)/isotropic = 5/2 face-on, 5/16 edge-on. (5) h_tree = 4.3359e-48 reproduced (L_GW = 1.2250e-22 W); face-on peak 6.8556e-48, edge-on peak 3.4278e-48; if bits/s ~ (peak/h_n)^2 the 26.62-order EM-over-bulk gap lies in [26.22, 26.82] depending on the unspecified rod orientation. (6) D/lambda = 4.27e9, l/lambda = 1.06e-5, v/c = 1.67e-5: far-zone and slow-motion hypotheses hold. Out of scope, recorded only: a uniform 100 m rod at 100 rad/s carries peak tensile stress ~ rho Omega^2 l^2/8 = 9.8e10 Pa at steel density -- a design-point observation on the source, not on this formula.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. The flux formula is a theorem of linearised GR (Isaacson averaging), not a fit: it has no empirical input beyond c and G, and it is a closed-form identity that is machine-checked here against the quadrupole luminosity. Data that came later and bear on it: (i) the Hulse-Taylor and double-pulsar orbital decay and (ii) LIGO-Virgo strain measurements from 2015 on are tests of the quadrupole emission/flux chain in the strong-source regime; neither was READ this pass, so neither is offered as evidence either way. (iii) GW170817's bound |v_gw - c|/c <= 7e-16 -- READ elsewhere in the tree (manyc.GW170817_BOUND_HI, branelink.py:132) -- supports the massless-at-c hypothesis the formula's retarded time t - r/c presumes, on the 4D side. What the tree lacks is not a datum the formula's authors lacked but two specifications of its own: the orientation of the rod's spin axis relative to the Proxima line (moves h by a factor between sqrt(5/16) and sqrt(5/2) in rms, sqrt(5/8) to sqrt(5/2) in detector-seen peak) and which amplitude h denotes. Neither moves the conclusion: the EM link beats the bulk link by 26.22 to 26.82 orders instead of 26.62. On the bulk-graviton branch the question whether a 5D bulk graviton's energy at omega = 200 rad/s is carried by the 4D zero mode is not addressed by the 4D formula and is not tested here. Evidence neither way that earlier physicists' missing data changes this result.
grade_evidence: The published flux F = c^3/(16 pi G)<hdot_+^2 + hdot_x^2> (Maggiore eq. 1.153, READ via Gerosa GGI-2026 L01 p.5) is reproduced and machine-checked: with branelink's own rod quadrupole it integrates to the (2/45) G M^2 l^4 Omega^6/c^5 luminosity exactly, and the tree's h = (2/(D w)) sqrt(G L/c^3) reproduces 4.3359e-48. But the tree's single-h form holds on a smaller class than its use states: (a) it is exact only for h^2 = <h_+^2 + h_x^2> (circular polarisation, or total rms), and is 2x high in flux for a linear wave of peak h -- a polarisation hypothesis the owner (branelink.py:204-206, 209-211) drops; (b) it uses isotropic emission for a source whose pattern is proven anisotropic here (flux ratio 5/2 face-on to 5/16 edge-on, check 4b), so h is the sky-rms, not the strain at Proxima, and the rod's orientation is unspecified. No computed contradiction: no moved datum and no orientation moves the conclusion (EM over bulk: 26.22-26.82 orders vs the seated 26.62). Not WRONG, not DATA-DEPENDENT. Caveat on the reading: the source is a lecture-notes restatement of a textbook equation, not a refereed arXiv paper, because every arXiv route was down this pass.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owner names h as the sky-rms total strain sqrt(<<h_+^2 + h_x^2>>) (or the face-on circular peak with the 5/2 factor) and states that isotropy is used as a sky average for an anisotropic source. To OPEN: a reading of Maggiore 1.153 / Isaacson 1968 / arXiv:0903.0338 at source that disagreed with the Gerosa restatement's coefficient (improbable: check 1 fixes the coefficient by the quadrupole luminosity). To WRONG: only a computed contradiction of the flux identity itself, e.g. a failure of check 1 -- none found. A specified rod orientation would replace the [26.22, 26.82] range with a single figure, not change the grade.
